task: Recover safely from a qrexec crash after a durable coordinator mutation but before DurableRequestJournal commit, without replaying unsafe mutations.

attempts: Replay every pending request after restart.
Infer success for every operation from current mission state.
Reconcile only operations with an exact durable postcondition that is already idempotent under the same worker, fencing token, and payload.
correctness.selected: Reconcile pending complete requests only when durable mission state is completed with the same missionId, workerId, leaseToken, and deeply equal result; keep claim/heartbeat/fail indeterminate.
correctness.reason: MissionQueue.complete is already idempotent for the exact committed result and fencing token. claim may select another mission, heartbeat changes lease time, and fail changes attempts/ownership, so current state cannot causally prove those requests without a new transactional receipt.

attempts: Treat a pending journal entry as success after any matching-looking state.
Add an operation receipt to mission metadata immediately.
Use read-only postcondition reconciliation and fail closed on ambiguity.
robustness_security.selected: Read-only reconciliation under the existing per-request process-spanning lock; commit the journal only after exact postcondition proof.
robustness_security.reason: This preserves lease fencing and prevents a retry from mutating mission state again. Ambiguous pending claim/heartbeat/fail requests remain blocked instead of being guessed or replayed.

attempts: Introduce a transactional database/WAL spanning mission state and request outcomes.
Add a new reconciliation daemon or qrexec round-trip.
Reuse the existing MissionCoordinator read path only when a pending complete request is encountered.
latency_resources_regression.selected: Reuse the existing local durable store and coordinator get() path only on the rare pending-complete recovery path.
latency_resources_regression.reason: Normal requests add zero extra qrexec round-trips and no new daemon or persistent service. The extra store read occurs only after a crash leaves a pending complete request.

positive: Crash after durable complete mutation leaves the request pending; retry reconciles from exact durable terminal state, commits the journal, and returns an attested completed response.
Reconciled completion does not create another mission or alter total mission count.
negative: Crash after durable claim remains indeterminate and retry does not claim a second mission.
requestId reuse with a different command remains rejected.
Coordinator rejections remain durably committed as deterministic attested error responses.

failures_lessons: A process-spanning request lock solves concurrent duplicate execution but not the mutation-to-journal crash window by itself.
Exactly-once cannot be claimed for claim/heartbeat/fail from current state alone; a future transactional operation receipt would be required to reconcile them causally.
Postcondition reconciliation is safe only where the production mutation is already exact-idempotent under the same fencing authority and payload.
safety: Synthetic/defensive transport qualification only. No real financial transactions, payment data, fraud workflows, or weakened security controls.
